claim: Replaying full multi-day conversation history on every inference call causes agents to hallucinate intermediate steps (inventing approvals that weren't given or skipping steps assumed completed) after long idle periods.
stance_target: idle agents need explicit, durable state rather than relying on chat-history replay to decide what to do after dormancy
scope_conditions: multi-day/multi-week agentic workflows (HR onboarding, invoice disputes, sales sequences)
quoted_support: When an agent pauses for three days waiting on a document signature, then resumes with a massive context dump, the model frequently hallucinates intermediate steps that never happened. It "remembers" approvals that weren't given or skips steps it assumes were completed.

claim: ADK's event-driven dormancy pattern lets a long-running agent container scale to zero entirely during idle periods, with session state persisted durably (SQLite/Cloud SQL) and resumed only when an external webhook fires.
stance_target: idle/dormant agents should fully terminate their compute process rather than poll or hold a blocked thread, relying on external event signals to restart
scope_conditions: Google ADK deployed on Cloud Run / Agent Runtime
quoted_support: Active polling wastes compute. Blocked threads don't scale. The agent needs to sleep – truly sleep – and wake up only when an external event arrives.

claim: ADK uses a state_delta mechanism where a webhook-triggered runner.run_async atomically applies a state transition before the agent's next inference call, avoiding replay of old conversation history.
stance_target: resumption after dormancy should be driven by atomic state transitions, not conversation replay
quoted_support: The key mechanism is state_delta. When the webhook fires, run_async atomically applies the state transition before the agent's next inference call.

claim: ADK golden evaluation tests can pre-seed session state to simulate a 48-hour idle delay and assert the agent correctly refuses to skip workflow steps when prompted to do so.
stance_target: safety-gate testing is needed to verify dormancy/resume logic does not silently skip or corrupt state
quoted_support: A second test case pre-seeds the state to IT_PROVISIONED and confirms the agent correctly resumes after a simulated 48-hour hardware delay, calling check_hardware_delivery and send_day_one_schedule in sequence without dropping the new hire's original context.

claim: Google's Agent Runtime (Vertex AI agent engine) handles session persistence and auto-scaling including scale-to-zero during idle time out of the box, with the same checkpoint-and-resume code working unchanged from local SQLite to managed cloud storage.
stance_target: production agent platforms now offer managed scale-to-zero dormancy as a built-in capability, not something teams must hand-roll
scope_conditions: Google Agent Runtime / Vertex AI agent engine
quoted_support: Agent Runtime handles session persistence, auto-scaling (including scale-to-zero during idle time), and Cloud Trace integration out of the box.

claim: Multi-agent delegation (narrow sub-agents with focused prompts and tool sets, e.g. a dedicated it_agent) keeps reasoning quality sharp even after weeks of accumulated state, versus a single monolithic agent carrying all workflow state and tools.
stance_target: specialized sub-agents outperform monolithic agents in long-running, multi-step workflows
quoted_support: Each agent has a focused prompt and a narrow tool set, which keeps reasoning sharp even after weeks of accumulated state.
